correctness.rationale: The product is the alternating determinant of the first two coordinates times z, including in characteristic two. The Rota–Baxter defect is alternating by direct evaluation on equal inputs, not by dividing by two. The three independent basis pairs give exactly the displayed ideal. The equations h²=j²=0 force h,j into the radical and leave f=det X−k(k+lambda). After the shift this is primitive linear in X22, with coprime coefficients over every field extension; it is geometrically prime and the reduction has dimension six. The Jacobian forces X=0 at a singular geometric point, and there k(k+lambda)=0 and 2k+lambda=0 give only the zero-weight plane, also in characteristic two. For the motivic formula one can split by whether the first column is zero: over nonzero first columns and arbitrary k, the second-column equation gives an affine-line bundle, locally trivial on the two nonzero-coordinate charts; a zero first column allows either one or two distinct k values and an arbitrary second column. Multiplication by the class of the two free central coordinates gives the two stated classes, and hence counts over all finite extensions and the zeta functions. At the nonzero-weight base point the full Jacobian has the two independent entries −lambda in the a direction and lambda in the h direction; the reduced Jacobian adds the j constraint. At weight zero the origin has full and reduced tangent dimensions 9 and 7. The exhibited j=t solution modulo t² satisfies every generator and cannot lift modulo t³ because j²=t² there, regardless of other second-order coefficients.

originality.rationale: Pass is for the full representing scheme and its explicit infinitesimal behavior relative to the reduction, not for the field-point classification, determinant locus or point-count transition in isolation. There is stronger overlap than the frozen discussion acknowledges: Resultary c77f6ea4e079 is exactly the same operator identity after changing the weight sign and using the associative product itself as an alternating Heisenberg Lie bracket. This equivalence works in every characteristic, over test algebras as well as fields. That record supplies the reduced equation, point counts, and the square equations as steps in a field-point proof; it does not prove that either of those coordinates is a nonzero nilpotent or analyze second-order lifts. Its explicit stratification also yields the motivic formulas by the same affine coordinate elimination, and the reduced smoothness calculation is a direct Jacobian computation from the known hypersurface. The genuine added result is that the full defining equations retain obstructed nilpotent directions even at a smooth reduction, with exact arbitrary-field proofs. No priority is inferred from the shared date of the records.
